lines.text: Why don't you dry out? Your skin has a brick wall.
lines.phonemes: wˌaɪ dˈəʊnt juː dɹˈaɪ ˈaʊt? jɔː skˈɪn hɐz ɐ bɹˈɪk wˈɔːl.

lines.text: Its outer layer, the stratum corneum, is the barrier. Flat dead cells are the bricks. Fats between them are the mortar. A scientist named Peter Elias called it that.
lines.phonemes: ɪts ˈaʊtə lˈeɪə, ðə stɹˈɑːtəm kˈɔːnɪəm , ɪz ðə bˈaɹiə. flˈat dˈɛd sˈɛlz ɑː ðə bɹˈɪks. fˈats bɪtwˌiːn ðˌɛm ɑː ðə mˈɔːtə. ɐ sˈaɪəntɪst nˈeɪmd pˈiːtə ɪlˈaɪəs kˈɔːld ɪt ðˈat.

lines.text: The mortar is stacked sheets of fat, wrapped around each cell. That makes a semi-permeable barrier, which is what lets life live on land.
lines.phonemes: ðə mˈɔːtəɹ ɪz stˈakt ʃˈiːts ɒv fˈat, ɹˈapt ɐɹˈaʊnd ˈiːtʃ sˈɛl. ðat mˌeɪks ɐ sˈɛmipˈɜːməbəl bˈaɹiə, wˌɪtʃ ɪz wɒt lˈɛts lˈaɪf lˈaɪv ˌɒn lˈand.

lines.text: That wall is the skin's first line of defence. It keeps outside things out and holds water in. It is not a single tough sheet. It is a system of cells, fats and acids.
lines.phonemes: ðat wˈɔːl ɪz ðə skˈɪnz fˈɜːst lˈaɪn ɒv dɪfˈɛns. ɪt kˈiːps aʊtsˈaɪd θˈɪŋz ˈaʊt and hˈəʊldz wˈɔːtəɹ ˈɪn. ɪt ɪz nˌɒtə sˈɪŋɡəl tˈʌf ʃˈiːt. ɪt ɪz ɐ sˈɪstəm ɒv sˈɛlz, fˈats and ˈasɪdz.

lines.text: Here is the twist. The bricks are not the tight part. Most dissolved substances pass through the cells more easily than through the fats.
lines.phonemes: hˈiəɹ ɪz ðə twˈɪst. ðə bɹˈɪks ɑː nˌɒt ðə tˈaɪt pˈɑːt. mˈəʊst dɪsˈɒlvd sˈʌbstənsɪz pˈas θɹuː ðə sˈɛlz mˈɔːɹ ˈiːzili ðɐn θɹuː ðə fˈats.

lines.text: So your skin's wall is bricks and fats, working as a team. The fats are the tight part.
lines.phonemes: sˌəʊ jɔː skˈɪnz wˈɔːl ɪz bɹˈɪks and fˈats, wˈɜːkɪŋ az ɐ tˈiːm. ðə fˈats ɑː ðə tˈaɪt pˈɑːt.

lines.text: Next: fingerprints, formed before birth. The pattern spreads in waves.
lines.phonemes: nˈɛkst: fˈɪŋɡəpɹˌɪnts, fˈɔːmd bɪfˌɔː bˈɜːθ. ðə pˈatən spɹˈɛdz ɪn wˈeɪvz.
